title: Sharp terminal edge count in random triangle removal
exact_target: For the process that repeatedly removes the three edges of a uniformly selected remaining triangle from $K_n$ until triangle-free, does the final edge count $F_n$ satisfy $E[(F_n/n^{3/2}-1/(2$ $\operatorname{sqrt}(2)))^2]->0$?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For the process that repeatedly removes the three edges of a uniformly selected remaining triangle from $K_n$ until triangle-free, does the final edge count $F_n$ satisfy $E[(F_n/n^{3/2}-1/(2$ $\operatorname{sqrt}(2)))^2]->0$?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For the process that repeatedly removes the three edges of a uniformly selected remaining triangle from $K_n$ until triangle-free, does the final edge count $F_n$ satisfy $E[(F_n/n^{3/2}-1/(2$ $\operatorname{sqrt}(2)))^2]->0$?
